title: Queries with select(): lookup, keyset pages, counts with zeros, an atomic like
problem: Implement four repository functions with SQLAlchemy 2.x statements: a user lookup, one page of chat history (newest first, paginated by id), member counts for every chat (including empty ones, with a tie-break), and an atomic like counter.
requirements: find_user returns the User or None
messages_page returns up to limit messages of one chat, highest id first; with before_id only ids below it
member_counts returns (title, count) for every chat, including chats with 0 members, sorted by count descending then title ascending
like adds 1 with one UPDATE whose SET clause computes likes + 1 in SQL, raises LookupError for a missing message, and doesn't commit
Use select()/update() statements, not raw SQL strings
contract: find_user(session, username) -> User | None; messages_page(session, chat_id, before_id=None, limit=20) -> list[Message]; member_counts(session) -> list[tuple[str, int]]; like(session, message_id) -> None
edgeCases: Last page shorter than limit, then an empty page
hints: Conceptual: write the SQL you'd use first (DB.M01-M02), then translate each clause: WHERE -> .where(), LEFT JOIN -> .outerjoin(), GROUP BY -> .group_by(). A Select can be extended step by step.

Specific: for zero counts you need an outer join and count(ChatMember.user_id), not count(*). For pagination add .where(Message.id < before_id) only when before_id is given. For like, look at update(...).values(...) with an expression and result.rowcount.
evaluation: One query per function (no Python-side filtering or sorting)
like doesn't load the Message object
